targetAudience: PMs choosing metrics for AI assistants
topic: Task success rate vs user satisfaction as the north-star metric for an AI assistant
coreInsight: Users rate how an AI answer feels, not whether it got the job done, so satisfaction can rise while task success falls; lead with task success wherever the outcome can be checked.

hookVariants.text: Your thumbs-up rate is lying to you.
CSAT or task success: which is your AI’s north star?

selectionRationale: Highest total (23/25): a paradox that stops the scroll, delivered by an illustrative comparison and a rule for choosing.

script.onScreen: PICK YOUR NORTH STAR / When to lead with each. / Task success when the job has a checkable outcome · Satisfaction when quality is a matter of taste · Define “success” per task before launch · Track both; investigate when they diverge / Rising CSAT + falling success = errors users can’t see.
script.voiceover: Lead with task success when the outcome can be checked, with satisfaction when quality is taste. Define success per task before launch, track both, and investigate when they split.

script.onScreen: Measure the outcome, not the mood. / Share this with your AI metrics owner
script.voiceover: Measure the outcome, not the mood. Share this with whoever owns your AI metrics.

caption:
A confident, friendly wrong answer often gets a thumbs up.

That’s why satisfaction and task success can move in opposite directions. Users rate how an answer feels; they often can’t tell whether it was right.

How to choose:
→ lead with task success when the job has a checkable outcome (booked, resolved, correct)
→ lead with satisfaction when quality is a matter of taste (tone, style)
→ track both, and treat a gap between them as a bug report

(The 82% vs 54% in the reel is an illustrative example, not data from a real product.)
